verdict.rationale: Inngest's core purpose is running background and scheduled jobs autonomously. It supports event triggers, timezone-aware cron schedules, automatic retries, durable checkpointing and long-running agent loops, and community users confirm relying on it for background processing, scheduling and queues. missing for 10: a no-code or natural-language way to set up automations (setup requires writing SDK functions in code), and the functions run on the user's own compute rather than Inngest-hosted execution.

support.subject: As an AI-native user, I can set up automations that run autonomously in the background

citations.quote: Write functions in TypeScript, Python or Go to power background and scheduled jobs, with steps built in. We handle the backend infra, queueing, scaling, concurrency, throttling, rate limiting, and observability for you.
Inngest's cron schedules also support timezones, allowing you to schedule work in whatever timezone you need work to run in.
If the agent needs to wait three hours for a human to approve something, it suspends entirely, holding zero resources, and resumes when the approval arrives.
We needed a scheduling, queue, trigger solution. The docs are fairly good and it worked after some fiddling with our setup.
With Inngest, I moved all of our background services and processing to a separate sub-repo, and we can develop, deploy and monitor entirely independently
